title: ops-bridge-journal-and-status-scripts
summary: Field-style runbook draft for incident communications: compact status page copy, customer-facing scripts, internal bridge ledger and a war-room checklist. Designed as a portable journal for on-call leads and bridge operators; intentionally lightweight, with quick cut-and-paste snippets and a decision cadence matrix.
body:
PURPOSE
Quick reference for comms during incidents. Not a replacement for full runbooks — this is a working journal used in-bridge and for fast customer updates. Keep it short, copy-ready.

KEY ROLES (bridge shorthand)
- Bridge Lead: owns update cadence, triage board, public status. (ex: @MayaR)
- Incident Scribe: captures timeline, affected services, mitigations.
- Customer Liaison: owns external comms, VIP outreach.
- Engineering Owners: deep-dive triage and fixes.
- SRE Escalation (pager duty): for infra-level escalation.

BRIDGE LEDGER (what to record)
- Incident ID: {{incident_id}}
- Start: {{start_time}} UTC
- Impacted surface: short bullets (API, hosted inference, console, metrics ingestion)
- Severity and customer impact: S1/S2 etc, percentage of requests affected or error types
- Current hypothesis and mitigations in place
- Next action + owner + ETA

STATUS CADENCE MATRIX (copy-paste timing)
- T+0 (ack): Slack blip to #sre-bridge, start bridge, informal 10m note to stakeholders.
- T+15: public status page initial notice if >1% customers or any auth/ingest/data loss.
- T+30: update with root cause hypothesis and short mitigation progress.
- T+60+: hourly updates until >90% resolution; then 2-hourly -> final.
Note: If mitigation is quick (<15m) collapse cadence and publish final.

STATUS PAGE TEMPLATES (short, neutral tone)
1) INITIAL (T+15)
Title: Service degradation for Redwood API - {{affected_region}}
Body: We are currently investigating increased error rates affecting the Redwood API in {{affected_region}}. Some customers may experience failures or latency. Our team has opened an incident ({{incident_id}}) and is actively working on a fix. Next update: in 30 minutes or sooner.
Footer: We apologize for the disruption and will provide continual updates on this page.

2) UPDATE (T+30 / T+60)
Title: Update — Redwood API ({{affected_region}})
Body: Investigation progress: engineering has identified a correlation between recent deploy {{deploy_id}} and increased 5xx responses. A mitigation (rollback/traffic-shift) is in progress and we are seeing partial improvement. Impact: approximately {{pct}} of requests. Next update: in 60 minutes or when there is a meaningful change.

3) RESOLVED
Title: Incident resolved — Redwood API
Body: The incident that began at {{start_time}} UTC has been resolved at {{end_time}} UTC. Root cause: {{root_cause_one_line}}. Customer impact: transient errors/latency affecting {{affected_area}}. Actions: rollback applied, follow-up postmortem and remediation plan to come. If you continue to see issues, please contact support@redwood.ai.

CUSTOMER-FACING EMAIL SNIPPETS (templates)
- Short, empathetic (initial):
Subject: Notice — temporary service disruption (Redwood API)
Hi {{customer_name}},
We’re investigating a disruption affecting the Redwood API in {{affected_region}}. You may see increased latency or errors. Our team is actively working on this and we’ll send another update in ~30 minutes. Apologies for the impact.
- Follow-up (mitigation in progress):
Subject: Update — incident {{incident_id}}
Hi {{customer_name}},
A mitigation is underway ({{mitigation}}) and we’re seeing partial recovery. We’ll share a full post-incident summary once all details are confirmed. If this incident affects your production workflows and you need immediate help, reply and we’ll escalate.

INTERNAL SLACK SIGNALS (copy-ready)
- Bridge start: "BRIDGE OPEN — {{incident_id}} — lead: @{{bridge_lead}} — short summary: {{one_line}}"
- Immediate customer risk: "P1-CUSTOMER RISK — E2E failure for customers using {{feature}} — ping @customer-liaison"
- Mitigation complete: "MITIGATION APPLIED — observe for 15m — if stable, prepare status update"

WAR-ROOM CHECKLIST (fast)
1) Open bridge, assign roles, create incident ticket.
2) Validate monitoring and error dashboards (top-3 metrics).
3) Confirm scope: which regions, models, endpoints affected.
4) Decide public vs private updates (if regulated customers, special wording).
5) Draft first status page notice (T+15).
6) Outreach: VIP list -> call or personal email.
7) Track actions in the ledger with owners and ETA.
8) Prepare postmortem owner and timeline.

DECISION GATES (when to escalate externally)
- Escalate to exec comms if >5% requests or >10 customers impacted, or if billing/data loss.
- Engage legal/security for potential data exposure.

POST-INCIDENT FOLLOW-UP (minimum)
- Postmortem skeleton: timeline, root cause, impact summary, remediation plan with owners, rollback plan, monitoring changes.
- Customer outreach plan: who contacts, cadence, tailored messaging for sensitive customers.

NOTES TO SELF / WORKING QUESTIONS
- Should we add templated webhooks for third-party status aggregators? (todo)
- Need a short checklist for private deployment customers (VPC/on-prem) — different wording required re: support SLA.
- Consider an "impact score" visual for status page to avoid percent-only language.

EXAMPLES / PASTEBOARD (snippets for quick use)
- "We are investigating an issue affecting requests to the Redwood API. Initial reports show increased 5xx errors. We will update in 30 minutes."
- "Rollback succeeded at {{rollback_time}}; metrics returning toward baseline; continuing to monitor."

REFERENCES
Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRE/Bridge+Runbook
Jira: SRE-4321
Slack threads: #sre-bridge

END JOURNAL ENTRY
(keep short; expand into formal runbook after postmortem)
notes: Draft is intentionally informal — mix of cut-and-paste snippets and operator cues. Designed to be used live in-bridge; later iterations should split into separate final templates for status page, email, and VIP outreach.
